title: BTS Opts Out of 2027 Grammys, Citing Concerns Over New 'Asian Pop' Category
summary: In a move that has sparked intense discussion among fans, BTS announced on July 29 that they will not submit their highly anticipated comeback album, ARIRANG, for consideration at the 2027 Grammy Awards. Each of the seven members shared the decision via individual Instagram Stories, accompanied by a statement: "We decided not to participate in the Grammys this year. We hope that music can be heard and loved by itself rather than being divided by region or language." The announcement comes just weeks after the Recording Academy unveiled a new category: Best Asian Pop Music Performance. Described as recognizing "artistic excellence in Asian pop music performances originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets, including but not limited to K-pop, J-pop and C-pop," the category has been praised by some as overdue recognition, but criticized by others as a potential form of segregation. BTS has been nominated for five Grammys since 2020, including for their English-language hits "Dynamite" and "Butter." However, their new album marks a return to a sound deeply rooted in their Korean identity and earlier musical style. In a recent Rolling Stone cover story, member Jin reflected, "I believed that our most beloved songs are our identity... our identity is in the music we used to make." The group's decision raises questions about whether ARIRANG would have been automatically funneled into the new Asian pop category rather than competing in general fields. BTS's statement suggests a desire to transcend such labels. They also drew inspiration from Bad Bunny, who made history by performing the Super Bowl halftime show in Spanish and winning Album of the Year with an all-Spanish album. RM noted, "All of the people in the world are watching Parasite... so if there's a chance, we definitely want to, some day." For now, BTS is choosing to sit out music's biggest night, prioritizing artistic integrity over potential trophies.
why_it_matters: BTS's refusal to participate highlights a deeper struggle over how the music industry values art from outside the English-speaking world — and raises questions for young listeners about whether awards that divide by region help or hurt the artists they love.

background_read: The Grammy Awards, held since 1959 by the Recording Academy (an organization of music professionals), have long faced criticism over categories that can isolate artists by race or language. In 2020, the Academy renamed the "Urban Contemporary" category after artists argued it was a euphemism for Black music.

The new Best Asian Pop Music Performance category echoes debates from the 1970s and 1980s, when the Grammys created separate "Latin" categories. While some Latin artists welcomed the visibility, others felt these categories segregated non-English music away from the general fields like Album of the Year.

BTS, a South Korean boy band that has become a global phenomenon, has already broken numerous barriers — including a Grammy nomination for their English-language hit "Dynamite." Their return to a more Korean-rooted sound with ARIRANG and their decision to sit out the 2027 ceremony follows a pattern of artists using their platform to challenge institutional labels.

RM's mention of "Parasite" — the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture at the Oscars, in 2020 — underscores a growing global appetite for content that doesn't fit neatly into Western boxes. Bad Bunny, a Puerto Rican rapper who famously performed the Super Bowl halftime show entirely in Spanish and won a Grammy for an all-Spanish album, set a similar precedent for letting art speak across language.

perspectives.description: A dedicated Asian pop category could give long-overdue recognition to artists working in K-pop, J-pop, and C-pop who rarely appear in general fields. It might create a platform for rising acts and help Asian pop gain industry respect.

Critics, including BTS, worry the category is a form of segregation that sidelines non-English work from major awards like Album of the Year. It may reinforce the idea that pop from Asia is a niche genre rather than part of the global mainstream.

Grammy categories have always been a double-edged sword: they can spotlight genres but also box them in. The same tension played out with Latin music awards decades ago, where visibility and ghettoization were debated simultaneously.

perspectives.perspective: Forward-looking (how this could reshape the Grammys)
perspectives.description: BTS's boycott could pressure the Recording Academy to rethink category structures and integrate non-English performances into general fields. If ARIRANG succeeds commercially without a Grammy push, it may prove that artistic integrity can outweigh institutional prizes.
